title: Fields and Properties
theory: A field stores data directly inside a class. A property provides a controlled way to read or change a value using get and set.
Keeping data private protects an object's internal state. A property can allow other code to read a value while only the class can change it.
Use properties when validation or controlled access matters, such as preventing a player's health from becoming negative.
terms: A controlled way to access data.
Accessible only within its containing class.
Protecting internal state behind a public interface.
tryIt: Create a Character class with a public Name property and a Health property that cannot be changed directly outside the class.
challenge: Add validation so TakeDamage cannot reduce Health below zero.
mistakes: Do not expose every field publicly without a reason.
private members cannot be accessed from unrelated classes.
A property is not the same as a method.
summary: Properties provide controlled access to data. Encapsulation protects object state and keeps values valid.
quiz: private limits access to the containing class.
Properties expose controlled get and set operations.
The class controls assignment while readers can still access it.
Encapsulation protects implementation details and state.
